chunks.arabic_text: بِاسْنَادِهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Via his chain from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' who said:

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا مَاتَ وَلَمْ يُوَصِّ فَرُفِعَ أَمْرُهُ إِلَى قَاضِي الْكُوفَةِ فَصَيَّرَ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ الْقَيِّمَ بِمَالِهِ وَكَانَ رَجُلًا خَلَفَ وَرَثَةً صِغَارًا وَمَتَاعًا وَجَوَارِي، فَبَاعَ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ الْمَتَاعَ فَلَمَّا أَرَادَ بَيْعَ الْجَوَارِي ضَعُفَ قَلْبُهُ فِي بَيْعِهِنَّ وَلَمْ يَكُنِ الْمَيِّتُ صَيَّرَ إِلَيْهِ وَصِيَّتَهُ وَكَانَ قِيَامُهُ بِهَا بِأَمْرِ الْقَاضِ لِأَنَّهُنَّ فُرُوجٌ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَقُلْتُ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ يَمُوتُ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا فَلَا يُوَصِّ إِلَى أَحَدٍ وَخَلَفَ جَوَارِي فِيُقِيمُ الْقَاضِي رَجُلًا مِنَّا لِبَيْعِهِنَّ أَوْ قَالَ يَقُومُ بِذَلِكَ رَجُلٌ مِنَّا فَيَضْعُفُ قَلْبُهُ لِأَنَّهُنَّ فُرُوجٌ فَمَا تَرَى فِي ذَلِكَ؟ فَقَالَ: إِذَا كَانَ الْقَيِّمُ مِثْلَكَ وَمِثْلَ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ فَلَا بَأْسَ

translations.en: A man from among our companions died and did not leave a will, so his case was referred to the judge of Kufa, who appointed Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim as the supervisor of his wealth. He was a man who left behind small children as heirs, household items, and slave-women. Abd al-Hamid sold the items, but when he wanted to sell the slave-women, his heart had misgivings about selling them because they were Furuj (had had a sexual relation with the master). The deceased had not appointed him as executor; his role was by the order of the judge because they were Furuj. Muhammad said: I mentioned this to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: May I be your ransom, a man from among our companions dies without appointing anyone as executor and leaves slave-women, so the judge appoints a man from among us to oversee their sale (or said: a man from among us takes charge of that), and his heart has misgivings because they are Furuj. What is your ruling on that? He said: If the supervisor is like you or like Abd al-Hamid, then there is no problem.

en.summary: This hadith clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a testamentary executor (wasi) and a court-appointed supervisor (qayyim), ruling that the latter's personal emotional attachment to the slave-women does not invalidate the sale. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the reliability (thiqa) of the appointed guardian, ensuring that the transaction remains valid even if the supervisor experiences hesitation due to the women's status as 'Furuj'.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling slave-women appointed by a judge if the supervisor has misgivings?

key_terms.قَيِّم: Supervisor or executor of an estate
key_terms.فُرُوج: Slave-women who have had sexual relations with their master
